title: The Movie Studio
victoryHeadline: Caught! It's a wrap, and so is she.
acts: Stage Nine of "Cutlass of the Damned" ran, as ever, on the general theory that if a sound is loud enough somebody will simply assume it's sound design. On the Western Set, Falcon had reached take nineteen of a quick-draw that ended, with impressive consistency, in him backing into the same cactus, while Johnny kept the camera rolling because — he insisted — posterity deserved the full data set. Two sets over, Cornelius was thirty-nine takes into a single Romance Set kiss, sunglasses on indoors as always, and Damara had stopped even trying to fight the real flowers props had ordered by mistake: every take ended in a sneeze so enormous it looked, on playback, exactly like heartbreak. Nobody watching the dailies later could say for certain whether she'd been crying or allergic, and Damara herself, to be fair, wasn't always sure either.

Out in the mud of the War Set, a smaller drama unfolded entirely on its own terms. Idris had been standing in the same puddle for two and a half hours of continuity and had begun, quietly, to keep count of how many close-ups Leeroy's death scene had racked up against his own total of zero, while Leeroy himself lay magnificently expired in the rubble, twitching at flies with a dedication Kobe — filming both of them from the corner — found increasingly hard to justify to his own patience. On the Horror Set, Gilbert cued a wave of static across the haunted television for what he was fairly sure was the eleventh time, privately delighted that a studio was finally paying him actual money to indulge the exact hobby that had once made him unemployable at school, while Hadako sat in the good chair beside the camera with her hair over her face, smiling at something underneath it that had nothing to do with the scene.

So when a short, sharp crash rolled across the lot from the direction of the trailers, followed by a sound the crew would later, independently and identically, describe as 'sproing', almost nobody looked up. Falcon assumed it was foley and went again on his quick-draw. Everywhere else on the lot, people made their own equally confident, equally wrong guesses, and carried on regardless. It took the tannoy's second announcement — calm, insistent, faintly apologetic — before anyone walked the length of the lot toward the Star Trailer, where the door hung very slightly ajar and the afternoon had, without anybody noticing the exact moment it happened, stopped being a normal day of filming.

whereabouts.A: Antonio spent the whole afternoon standing precisely to the left of the SciFi camera, beard tucked back, having been told three separate times that morning it was 'a lens flare issue' and choosing, wisely, not to ask a fourth.
whereabouts.B: Belah sat in Editing running her own dailies back frame by frame, absolutely convinced the effects team had shaved a good three inches off her tentacles out of spite, and quietly building a case.
whereabouts.C: Cornelius called for take thirty-nine of the same Romance Set kiss, insisting each one was 'nearly the one', sunglasses worn indoors as a matter of professional principle.
whereabouts.D: Damara stood among the real flowers props had ordered by mistake, sneezing through every take so violently it read, on playback, exactly like heartbreak — which it categorically was not.
whereabouts.E: Erik stayed flattened against the Epic Set's painted backdrop for the fourth hour running, his entire job description reduced to keeping one matte-painting seam out of frame.
whereabouts.F: Falcon drew on an imaginary opponent for the nineteenth time and backed, for the nineteenth time, into the same cactus, with an expression that suggested he still believed the twentieth would be different.
whereabouts.G: Gilbert cued static across the haunted television for what he'd lost count of as either the tenth or eleventh time, privately thrilled that a major studio was paying him to do the exact thing that had once got him sent to the school counsellor.
whereabouts.H: Hadako sat in the good chair beside the Horror Set camera, hair over her face as always, smiling at her phone underneath it about news she hadn't told anyone yet.
whereabouts.I: Idris stood in his mud puddle for the two-and-a-half-hourth instalment of continuity, keeping a private tally of close-ups he had never once been given.
whereabouts.J: Johnny kept the Western Set camera rolling through take after take, insisting, to anyone who'd listen, that posterity deserved the complete and unedited record.
whereabouts.K: Kobe worked the War Set camera from the corner, framing two grown men competing for who could suffer more picturesquely, and wondering, not for the first time, when exactly he'd agreed to this career.
whereabouts.L: Leeroy lay extravagantly dead in the rubble, twitching at every fly that landed on his forehead makeup with a commitment his co-star was starting to find personal.
whereabouts.M: Mason stood beside the catapult in a helmet whose visor had rusted shut that morning, unable to see a single thing, and had privately decided the professional move was simply not to mention it.
whereabouts.N: Natalia lay across the Star Trailer's stunt bed running her lines under her breath for a scene she still hadn't officially been given, in the one part of the whole lot where nobody was filming anything at all.
whereabouts.O: Olivia sat rigid under a hat the size of a card table while her freckles went on one by one, mentally rehearsing the patience she was fairly sure she'd need for the rest of the afternoon.
whereabouts.V: Vaughn paced his trailer floor beside the table, rehearsing a monologue about legacy that nobody, including him, entirely believed yet.

reveal: It was Natalia, in the Star Trailer, and the weapon was the bed. Weeks earlier, at Vaughn's insistence, Gilbert had quietly rigged its fold-away frame with a hydraulic release for a stunt shot that never actually got filmed — a bit of harmless props ingenuity he'd assumed had long since been forgotten about. Natalia hadn't forgotten. She lay beside Vaughn as he ran his monologue for the fourth time that hour, waited for the line she'd heard once too often, and eased the release exactly the way Gilbert had shown the stunt team months before. The bed did precisely what it had always been built to do — hard, fast, and once — and Vaughn went the rest of the way on his own momentum. Natalia straightened the sheets, resumed her rehearsal in a slightly lower voice, and was, by the time anyone opened the trailer door, still lying there looking entirely unbothered.

escape.generic: The studio wrote it off as a props malfunction, reshot the scene with a stunt dummy, and the real killer took a producer credit on the finished cut.

byAccused.A: Antonio's spot to the left of the camera stayed empty for the rest of the shoot, and the lens flare turned out — to nobody's surprise more than the crew's — to have had nothing to do with his beard at all.
byAccused.B: "Check the raw footage," Belah kept saying, all the way to the studio gate, "my tentacles were always this long" — which was true, and changed absolutely nothing.
byAccused.C: The Romance Set crew filmed Cornelius's own arrest in one continuous take, on his own strict instructions, and privately agreed it was the best performance he'd given all week.
byAccused.D: Damara never did get a clean take of that kiss, allergy or no allergy, and the real flowers were quietly swapped for silk ones the very next day — a mercy that arrived one arrest too late for her.
byAccused.E: Erik was hauled away from the backdrop still worrying, out loud, about the matte-painting seam, and nobody thought to tell him it no longer mattered in the slightest.
byAccused.F: Falcon was hauled off backing straight into the cactus one last time, protesting that a man who can't beat a plant hardly seems capable of anything worse.
byAccused.G: The studio's official report quietly credited Gilbert's old stunt-bed rig as 'a tragic mechanical fault', which was technically true, and let everyone who actually deserved a second look go on being watched by nobody.
byAccused.H: Hadako was hauled out of the good chair still smiling at whatever was on her phone, and never did tell the crew what the news had been.
byAccused.I: Idris's tally of zero close-ups became, on the six o'clock local news, exactly one — a small, deeply undeserved victory he'd have traded back in an instant.
byAccused.J: Johnny was hauled off the Western Set still insisting posterity deserved the full unedited footage, and got, in the end, rather more of it than he'd bargained for.
byAccused.K: "I was in the corner," Kobe told anyone who'd listen, "I'm always in the corner, ask anyone" — and several people did, and it didn't help at all.
byAccused.L: Leeroy was hauled up out of the rubble mid-death-scene, genuinely startled for the first time all day, while the fly that had been bothering him finally got some peace.
byAccused.M: Nobody on the Epic Set could get Mason's rusted helmet open to tell him he'd been arrested, and by several accounts he only found out during processing, muffled and three questions behind.
byAccused.O: Olivia's freckles were left half-finished, one cheek adventurous and one perfectly plain, and the continuity department never did let anyone live that down.
